newsitem.title: CHINA: Trader Toepfer blasts China corn losses report.
newsitem.headline: Trader Toepfer blasts China corn losses report.

text.p: Toepfer, One of Asia's major corn trading houses, denied on Friday a news agency report it had lost money on large sales of Chinese corn to South Korea.
"These are groudless rumours," Kim In-sung, manager of the Seoul office of Toepfer International told Reuters.
"So far, we have no record of failing to honour contracts with our clients," he said of the report which said the firm had been caught short on the Chinese sales.
"It's absolute garbage, it's nonsense, it's unsubstantiated," a senior Toepfer grain trader said.
"The statement that we are losing millions is false," he told Reuters from Singapore, where the company's Chinese corn trading business is controlled.
South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) has bought a total of 110,500 tonnes of Chinese corn since January. Out of the total purchase, NLCF bought 62,500 tonnes from Toepfer.
The Korea Feed Association (KFA) in Pusan also recently bought 74,000 tonnes of Chinese corn from Toepfer.
"We heard the rumours that Toepfer has been caught short on sales of Chinese corn," a trader with NLCF said.
"But we have not been asked by Toepfer to change the origin of our corn purchases," he added.
A senior KFA official said: "We do not care about the rumours since Toepfer has traded a lot of Chinese corn and has built up a good record so far."
The Toepfer trader in Singapore said the regional market for Chinese corn had heated up, with U.S. and Argentine-origin prices rising in recent weeks.
Corn is now loading in the northern Chinese port of Dalian at a minimum of $133-$134 a tonne free on board (FOB), he said.
The freight cost to small South Korean ports is around $10 a tonne, he added, bringing the C&F (cost and freight) price to about $143-$144 a tonne.

The South Korean KFA purchase was made in three shipments -- 14,000 tonnes at $141.40 a tonne C&F for arrival in Pusan port on May 25, and two shipments of 30,000 tonnes each at $139.90 C&F for arrival in Ulsan port by May 25 and June 25.
By contrast, U.S. corn is currently valued at $126 a tonne FOB, with freight to Asia at $24-25 a tonne, bringing the C&F price up to $150-151 a tonne to Japan and South Korea.
Argentine corn is a few dollars a tonne cheaper, with Chinese corn below even that, the Singapore-based trader said.

"So now Chinese corn is definitely cheaper than U.S," he said, adding that as the U.S. product arrived in Panamax size vessels carrying upwards of 50,000 tonnes, Chinese corn had the advantage of loading into smaller vessels more suitable for less developed Asian ports.
"So there is a big advantage to the Chinese maize (corn) right now," he said.

"The product is good. We've seen some samples from earlier shipments and the quality looks good. So overall there should be no problem trading Chinese maize -- if the Chinese continue to be willing sellers."
-- Lynne O'Donnell, Shanghai newsroom, (+86 21 6279-8544)
-- Jae Hur, Seoul newsroom, (+82 2 727-5651)
